title: Billing/metering: distinguish Dedicated committed throughput vs burst consumption in usage export
creator: Nadia Rahman
description:
Goal
Ensure Redwood’s billing + usage exports for Dedicated can clearly separate:
1) usage covered by the customer’s committed Dedicated capacity ("committed") and
2) any usage served above that commitment under the tier’s burst policy ("burst").

Why
- Sales/CS needs a clean story for “what you bought” vs “what you burst into” (recurring confusion in support + procurement).
- Finance needs accurate attribution for GM modeling and discount guardrails.
- Product tiering depends on consistent definitions across SLO dashboards and invoices.

Background / context
Dedicated tiers (Standard/Plus/Premium) include different entitlements around burst and overload behavior. As we roll out tier-aware admission control and routing, the same deployment may intermittently serve requests from (a) committed pool capacity and (b) shared burst pool (or temporary headroom within the dedicated pool). Customers are already asking how burst appears on invoices and whether “SLO misses” correlate with billing (it shouldn’t).

Scope
- Emit canonical metering events that attribute tokens (and optionally requests) to either committed or burst.
- Persist attribution end-to-end through:
  - internal billing ledger
  - customer usage export (CSV/Parquet + Usage API)
  - Finance reporting tables
- Add enough dimensions to support invoice line items and internal analysis: deployment_id, customer_id/org_id, tier, region, model, committed_vs_burst.

Non-goals
- Changing price books, list prices, or discounting logic.
- Re-defining the throughput SLO metric (this is billing attribution only).
- Retroactive backfill for historical invoices (unless Finance requests for a specific customer dispute).

Definitions
- committed: usage served against the customer’s reserved Dedicated capacity (their allocated pool/shape).
- burst: usage served above the committed entitlement under the tier’s burst policy (e.g., spillover to burst pool or temporary headroom). Burst may be billed separately or shown as $0 depending on contract; this ticket only ensures it’s measurable.

Proposed event schema (logical)
Metering event (per request, aggregated in pipeline):
- timestamp
- org_id
- deployment_id
- region
- model
- tier (string, e.g., standard|plus|premium)
- usage_type (enum): committed | burst
- input_tokens
- output_tokens
- total_tokens
- request_count (optional, for non-token endpoints)

Usage export changes
- Add column: dedicated_usage_type (committed|burst) for Dedicated deployments.
- Add column: dedicated_tier (standard|plus|premium) (mirrors control plane config at time of serving).
- Maintain existing columns for model, endpoint/route, region, tokens, timestamps.

Attribution rules (implementation notes)
- Source of truth for tier + pool mapping should come from the routing decision at serve time (avoid re-deriving from config later).
- usage_type should be set at admission/routing time based on whether request consumed committed capacity vs burst capacity.
- For failover scenarios (e.g., region failover): still attribute by usage_type. Region dimension should reflect where it was actually served.
- Streaming accounting: ensure total_tokens equals the same canonical token accounting used elsewhere (avoid the double-counting bug class we saw in streaming metrics).

Acceptance criteria
1) For a Dedicated deployment, usage export includes dedicated_usage_type and dedicated_tier populated for 99.9%+ of rows (remaining rows allowed only during rollout window / feature flag off).
2) Sum(committed tokens) + Sum(burst tokens) == Sum(total tokens) for a deployment over any selected window (within expected late-arriving events tolerance).
3) Billing ledger can generate separate rollups by usage_type for Finance and invoicing.
4) Docs / internal runbook note how to interpret committed vs burst in exports, and how it relates (and does not relate) to throughput SLO credits.

Testing / validation plan
- Shadow-compare per-deployment totals against existing usage export totals for 7 days in staging and 3 days in prod (flag on for internal orgs only).
- Synthetic load test: generate controlled “burst” by throttling committed pool capacity and verifying attribution flips as expected.
- Validate dimensions (tier, deployment_id, region, model) are stable and not null.

Rollout
- Feature-flag metering emission by org_id.
- Turn on for internal orgs + 1–2 beta Dedicated customers (coordinate with CS).
- After 1 week with clean totals, enable by default for all Dedicated deployments.

Stakeholders
- Metering/Billing: Cole Summers (assignee), Nadia Rahman (creator)
- Product (Dedicated tiers): Lauren Bishop
- Finance/FP&A: Laura Bennett, Rishi Malhotra
- Observability: Allison Grant (ensure usage_type dimension aligns with dashboards)

References
- Related PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-19380-add-burst-capacity-metering.json
- Related support ticket: SUP-18477 (burst policy confusion / billing question)
- Related work: ENG-19263 (tier→pool mapping), ENG-19244 (deployment throughput metrics)
